basic.title: Opening, Wheel, And The First Turn
basic.description: The formal opening resolves hand limit, the shared wheel push, one hand action, and one wheel-result action.

steps.welcome: Seven Hatreds has three victory paths: control 16 regions at New Year, capture an opponent's capital, or reach 3 prestige first.
steps.handLimit: At the start of every turn, check hand limit first. Ming may keep 15 cards; Later Jin and the Mongols may keep 10. Pick the excess card from the hand area and confirm the discard.
steps.handResource: Cards are your main resource. Event cards resolve when played, armament cards need one extra discard, tactic cards are used only in battle, and silver cards serve only as payment.
steps.wheelFirst: After the hand-limit check, the shared wheel is next. It has not moved yet. Moving it by 1, 2, or 3 spaces decides whether other players draw and which wheel-result action this turn will use.
steps.wheelMove: Now choose how far to push the shared wheel. This is only the wheel push, not the wheel-result action; use the free 1-space move for the smallest example.
steps.afterWheel: Once the shared wheel push is resolved, this turn still has two parts left: one hand action and one wheel-result action. The current player chooses which of those two parts to do first.
steps.pickAction: Hand action: Grant Pardon. Choose the action first, not a map region; the target troop and receiving Ming region are chosen in the next step.
steps.chooseGrantPardonTarget: Choose the pardon target on the map: click Shanhaiguan to move 1 Later Jin troop out of Jinzhou into that adjacent Ming-controlled region.
steps.payCards: The target is locked. Now discard 3 cards to pay for Grant Pardon; the map changes only after payment resolves.
steps.actionResult: Jinzhou loses an enemy troop, and Shanhaiguan gains a Ming troop. Hand resources have turned into direct board control.
steps.moraleLevel: The number on each troop is both level and morale. Higher level means stronger dice in battle; only when a troop falls to 0 does it rout away.
steps.wheelAction: The wheel-result action is now resolved. Wherever the shared wheel lands, it takes you into Reclaim and Farm, Diplomacy and Hire, Attack and Dispatch, or Recruit and Train.
steps.finish: The first-turn skeleton is: check hand limit, push the shared wheel, then complete one hand action and one wheel-result action.

attackAndBattle.title: Attack And Field Battle
attackAndBattle.description: Attack dispatch covers troop movement, tactic timing, damage assignment, and retreat after field battle.

steps.overview: Attack dispatch does not end when you click a target. You first move troops into place, and only after movement is done are the battles settled together.
steps.moveEntry: This time you enter from Attack and Dispatch. Move the troops into place first, and remember that the border also decides how many troops can actually deploy. Artillery and infantry move 1 region; cavalry move 2, and that distance can double if they stay inside friendly control and do not join battle.
steps.borderWidth: Once the target is chosen, the border limits how many troops can deploy. Mountains, rivers, walls, and cities all change the width of the field battle.
steps.battleOpen: Battles first reveal both sides' troops, then check whether either side plays a tactic card. This is the real timing window for tactics, and only after that do artillery, cavalry, and infantry resolve in order.
steps.tacticWindow: Tactic cards are not cards you casually throw at any time. In most battles you play only one, and this is the moment that changes how this fight trades.
steps.battleDamage: The total rolled in one combat stage deals 1 damage for every 3 points. Damage usually goes onto higher-level troops first, and artillery does not absorb losses for other units.
steps.battleResult: Field battle only compares the surviving infantry and cavalry. If those totals tie, the defender wins.
steps.retreatAndDefeat: After losing, you retreat into an adjacent controlled or friendly region and choose between rear guard and rout. The loser also takes a defeat marker that waits for Midyear character checks.
steps.finish: A real field-battle chain is movement, troop reveal, the tactic window, damage, victory, and retreat together, not just clicking a destination region.

siege.title: Siege And Occupation
siege.description: Siege covers defender city withdrawal, city battle resolution, and the post-victory choice between siege and occupation.

steps.overview: City battle is not the same as field battle. Defenders can fall back into the city, and even victory does not grant control immediately.
steps.defendCity: When a city region is attacked, up to 2 troops and 2 population can withdraw into the city. The choice decides what stays inside and what remains outside.
steps.cityBattle: City battle resolves artillery first, then cavalry and infantry together in melee. Cavalry also suffers a -1 penalty here.
steps.cityResult: If the defenders lose inside the city, those defenders are cleared, but control still depends on whether you besiege or occupy next.
steps.besiegeChoice: Besieging means leaving pressure outside the city while the defender still keeps regional control for now.
steps.occupyChoice: Only after every city is taken and you choose occupation does the region truly change control.
steps.finish: A city battle closes not on whether you won the fight, but on what state the city ends up in.

retreatAndRout.title: Retreat And Rout
retreatAndRout.description: The field-battle loser chooses between rear guard and rout.

steps.overview: After losing a battle, you must choose one retreat mode: rear guard or rout.
steps.chooseRout: Choose one retreat mode. This resolution uses rout.
steps.routResult: After routing, the source region is cleared of the defeated force and Ming gains 1 more defeat marker.
steps.finish: Rear guard leaves a remnant behind; rout loses more troops.

cavalryPlunder.title: Cavalry Plunder
cavalryPlunder.description: Cavalry can switch to plunder: take artillery/cavalry counterfire first, then plunder population with surviving cavalry and retreat.

steps.overview: Cavalry in field battle does not always have to make a normal attack. When the conditions are right, it can declare plunder.
steps.choosePlunder: Click the real cavalry plunder button. This sample plunders the defender deck, then removes population, draws cards, and retreats the cavalry.
steps.plunderResult: The plunder result is now in the resolution summary: population was removed, and the deck and hand changed together.
steps.finish: Cavalry plunder is a real pending-battle entry, not just an after-the-fact note.

cavalryEvasion.title: Cavalry Evasion
cavalryEvasion.description: Defending cavalry can leave a field battle for an adjacent friendly region without being treated as routed.

steps.overview: Cavalry can also evade in field battle. Once the defenders leave, the original battle still resolves whether the attacker breaks through.
steps.chooseEvasion: Click the real cavalry evasion destination. This sample retreats to an adjacent friendly region.
steps.evasionResult: The evasion result is now in the resolution summary: cavalry leaves the battle and enters the retreat destination.
steps.finish: Cavalry evasion is a real pending-battle entry, not a waterway note or post-battle retreat explanation.

neutralInvasion.title: Neutral Invasion
neutralInvasion.description: When you attack an unoccupied neutral region with population, neutral defenders are generated for the battle.

steps.overview: Neutral regions are not always empty. If a region has population but no troops, dispatching an attack can generate neutral defenders during resolution.
steps.resolveNeutral: Click the real pending-resolution button. This sample attacks Tumed, where population becomes neutral defenders.
steps.neutralResult: The resolution summary now records neutral defenders: the attacker did not break through, so the region stays neutral.
steps.finish: Neutral invasion is a battle-resolution rule, not just a map note. Control changes only if the attack actually breaks through.

waterDispatch.title: Water Dispatch
waterDispatch.description: Ming can dispatch through anchor-region sea routes; cavalry dispatch can reach farther, but each sea route still commits at most 2 troops.

steps.overview: Water movement is not just a map note. This sample relieves Dongjiang from Pidao through a real coast/sea-route dispatch candidate, and shows that a sea route can only continue through sea routes.
steps.chooseWaterTarget: Click Dongjiang in the real dispatch candidates. The option shows coast/sea route, cost 2, and limit 2; follow-up candidates do not turn a sea route into a land route.
steps.waterBoundary: The pending battle is now locked to the sea-route boundary: even with cavalry dispatch, this sea route has battle width 2 and commits at most 2 troops.
steps.finish: Water dispatch has entered the real pending-resolution chain; breakthrough still follows normal battle resolution.

wheelSharedCost.title: Wheel Branches And Development Actions
wheelSharedCost.description: Longer shared-wheel movement refills opponents and lands the turn in attack, dispatch, diplomacy, or hiring systems.

steps.overview: The shared-wheel push is never free. The farther you move, the more cards your opponents recover, and the more it changes this turn's landing gate.
steps.chooseMove: Pick the shared-wheel move "All opponents draw 2, move 3." This is still the wheel push, not the fight itself.
steps.drawResult: After the shared wheel moves 3 spaces, both the Mongols and Later Jin each draw 2 cards.
steps.dispatchReady: Once that cost is paid, this turn's wheel-result action is Attack / Dispatch. The point here is not to fight immediately, but to see how the shared wheel brings you into another system gate.
steps.finish: The shared wheel does more than move a few spaces. It decides which wheel-result action this turn will enter, and who gets cards back because of that push.

wheelReclaim.title: Wheel Reclaim
wheelReclaim.description: Wheel Reclaim directly adds population to a controlled region.

steps.overview: Reclaim is not an off-turn bonus. It is a formal wheel result.
steps.chooseMove: Move the wheel forward 1 for free and enter Reclaim.
steps.result: Once the wheel lands on Reclaim, it directly adds 1 population to a controlled region. Population later decides taxes, supply, and how much force you can sustain.
steps.finish: Reclaim matters because it thickens the base for later taxes and supply before it gives you more troops.

wheelMilitaryFarm.title: Wheel Military Farm
wheelMilitaryFarm.description: Wheel Military Farm adds both cards and troops.

steps.overview: Military Farm differs from Reclaim because it converts that base directly into current cards and troops.
steps.chooseMove: Move the wheel forward 1 more space and enter Military Farm.
steps.result: Wheel Military Farm draws 2 cards and then builds 1 level-2 regular troop. It increases both resources and live board presence.
steps.finish: Military Farm is one of the wheel's clearest snowball actions: your hand grows and your regular force rises with it.

wheelRecruitTrain.title: Wheel Recruit And Train
wheelRecruitTrain.description: Wheel Recruit / Train adds troops and trains artillery by armament level.

steps.overview: Wheel Recruit / Train is not only about placing new blocks. It also consumes the armament levels you have already developed.
steps.chooseMove: Move the wheel forward 1 more space and enter Recruit / Train.
steps.result: Wheel Recruit / Train directly builds 2 level-2 regular troops. If Artillery Technology has already advanced, existing artillery is trained upward at the same time.
steps.finish: This shows the wheel is not just rotating through labels. It is tying armaments, troop growth, and the live front together in one real result.

armamentUpgrade.title: Armament Upgrade
armamentUpgrade.description: Armament upgrade spends hand cards and updates the armament level on the live board.

steps.overview: Armaments do not grow for free. You still spend hand cards to push them higher.
steps.chooseAction: Play this armament card to enter Armament Upgrade. You still discard 1 more hand card before that armament rises by 1 level.
steps.payCards: Pick 2 cards from the hand at the bottom, then confirm the action.
steps.result: The upgrade is now live: Ming Artillery Technology has gone from level 1 to level 2, and the armament summary in the player strip updates with it.
steps.finish: This hand action does not change the map directly. It improves the armament level that later battles will use.

eventAction.title: Khan's Edict
eventAction.description: Khan's Edict is the Mongol faction action. It resolves through payment, effect choice, and result, with the discard and map change landing together.

steps.overview: Mongol faction actions are also paid with hand cards. Khan's Edict turns this action into recruit/training or diplomacy/hire.
steps.chooseAction: Click the Khan's Edict faction action on the right. After it starts, discard 1 hand card to enter the effect choice.
steps.payCards: Pick 1 card from the hand at the bottom, then confirm the action.
steps.chooseEffect: Click Shanhaiguan on the map first to confirm where Khan's Edict will add troops, then choose Recruit / Train to resolve the gain.
steps.result: The result has landed: Khan's Edict raised Mongol troops at Shanhaiguan from 2 to 4, so this action has already changed live board strength.
steps.finish: That is the faction-action rhythm: spend a card to fire it, then let the action effect change the live position immediately.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy And Hire
diplomacy.description: Enter a real wheel diplomacy step and see control markers and hired troops resolve together.

steps.overview: Diplomacy decides regional relationships, not just marker sides; hiring decides where new troops can appear.
steps.wheelEntry: Push the wheel into Diplomacy and Hire. This branch resolves control relationships and room for troops, not battle.
steps.chooseTarget: Diplomacy targets map regions. Click a region adjacent to your controlled areas; you cannot target homeland regions without control markers, Korea regions, or areas with regular troops stationed there.
steps.friendlyMark: Click Ningyuan on the map to place a friendly marker. A reverse-side marker means your troops may pass through and station there, but it is not yet a controlled region.
steps.tributeMark: Flip the friendly marker you just placed into a vassal marker. Only a face-up marker counts as your controlled region; neutral regions taken by battle also become this state directly.
steps.removeMark: Click Dongjiang on the map and remove the existing rival control marker. Diplomacy not only places your own markers; it can also push back markers already placed by someone else.
steps.hireOnly: Mercenary troops can only be built in controlled regions. They do not appear freely in ordinary neutral territory.
steps.finish: When diplomacy and hiring resolve together, you get two benefits at once: map relationships change, and force structure changes with them.

yearAndCharacters.title: Midyear, New Year, And Chronology
yearAndCharacters.description: Midyear taxes, character checks, New Year maintenance, attrition, chronology scoring, and turn-order refresh form the yearly resolution.

steps.overview: When the shared wheel reaches Midyear and New Year, the consequences of the whole year catch up together. Seven Hatreds does not care only about the move in front of you.
steps.midyearTax: Midyear checks taxes first: controlled regions with more population than troops send resources back into your hand, while besieged regions do not.
steps.midyearCharacters: Then come character checks. Eligible characters roll for resolution, and defeat markers are processed one by one during the character check.
steps.advanceNewYear: After Midyear, push on into New Year.
steps.newYearTribute: New Year Korean tribute: whoever controls Korean regions draws the matching number of Korea cards shown on the map.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Then comes fortification maintenance. If the Great Wall, Shanhaiguan, Ningyuan, or Jinzhou cannot be maintained, they fall into ruin and their border and city effects fail with them.
steps.newYearAttrition: After maintenance you still resolve attrition. If population cannot support the troops, you either discard to keep them or cut them yourself.
steps.chronologyScore: Chronology cards are not just year markers. The player with the highest score must pay half their hand to claim that year's prestige, or pass the chance to the next player.
steps.turnOrderRefresh: Once chronology resolves, both turn order and new characters refresh, and next year's tempo changes with them.
steps.finish: When a year ends, what you lose and gain is never just a few cards. The map's resources, characters, and order are all reshuffled.

koreaSpecial.title: Korea And Special Map Rules
koreaSpecial.description: Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan are map-specific rules that directly change play.

steps.overview: Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan are not side notes. They directly change scoring, movement, and defense.
steps.koreaRegion: First look at how New Year tribute already resolves. Whoever controls Korean regions actually draws the marked Korea cards into hand.
steps.hanseongVp: Hanseong is more than another region. Once Ming loses its initial control, whoever controls Hanseong effectively gains 1 extra prestige, and that prestige shows up directly on the player track.
steps.waterLimit: Sea routes between anchor regions can move at most 2 troops at a time, and cavalry cannot use sea routes to evade battle.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Now resolve New Year maintenance once. After fortifications are handled, troops in Korea also go through upkeep attrition.
steps.koreaAttrition: Korean regions provide no population support. Troops left in Korea must be paid entirely with cards during New Year, or Korea attrition removes them directly.
steps.shanhaiguan: Shanhaiguan is both a city and a special border between Jizhen and Liaoxi. While it stands, the border stays narrow; once ruined, that border collapses into open plain.
steps.finish: These are not optional notes. They are formal rules that directly decide whether you can hold, defend, or seize key prestige.
